A congenital blockage (bony, membranous, or mixed) of the posterior nasal opening, causing nasal obstruction. It may be unilateral or bilateral. Neonates are obligate nasal breathers; therefore, complete bilateral choanal atresia is a medical emergency requiring immediate oral airway support until surgical creation of a patent nasal airway. Early recognition and referral are critical in bilateral cases. Always assess for associated anomalies (e.g., CHARGE syndrome).

Nose bleeding is a condition which is common in adults. It may be due to a local cause in the nasal cavity (e.g., trauma, tumor, foreign body, septal varices, or septal deviation); or a systemic cause (e.g., blood disorders, vascular disorders, renal failure, hepatic failure, or use of anticoagulants (warfarin, heparin). Most cases of epistaxis are minor; do not require hospitalization. Patients with significant nose bleeding do require hospitalization.
